text.title: Red squirrel
text.menu_sub: Bound through the forest, find berries, dodge foxes.
text.intro_safe: Safe mode: explore! Bound through the forest and find berries.
text.intro_survival: Keep your food and warmth up. At night, sleep high in a spruce, like a squirrel in its drey.
text.intro_wild: Foxes hunt squirrels, but they can't climb. Run up a tree!
text.night_hint: It's night. Run at a spruce trunk to climb it, then sleep in its thick branches.
text.too_exposed: Too exposed to sleep! Climb a spruce and curl up in its thick branches.
text.sheltered: You're curled up safe and warm in the spruce branches.
text.hungry: You're hungry. Look for cones under the spruces, or berry bushes.
text.no_food: Nothing to eat here. Look for cones under the spruces, or berry bushes.
text.rain_start: It's starting to rain. Climb into a spruce's thick branches to stay warm.
text.chased: A fox is chasing you! Run up a tree!
text.about_looks: Red-brown fur, a long bushy tail and tufts on its ears. In winter its coat turns greyer and the ear tufts grow longer.
text.about_food: Spruce seeds from cones, buds, berries and mushrooms.
text.about_home: Builds a drey, a ball of twigs lined with moss, high up in a spruce. Sometimes it lives in a hole in a tree.
text.about_winter: Stays awake. It eats the seeds it hid in autumn, and on very cold days it stays in its drey.
text.about_young: Babies are born in the drey in spring, and often a second litter in summer.
text.about_fact: In autumn a squirrel dries mushrooms on branches, to eat later in winter.

year.shelter: Builds a drey (a ball of twigs lined with moss and lichen) high in a spruce, or uses a tree hole. Stays in it for days in hard frost.
year.young: Born in April–May, often a second litter in June–July.

food.autumn: Spruce seeds; hides seeds and dries mushrooms on branches for winter.
food.winter: Spruce cone seeds and its hidden stores.

year.notes: Its coat turns greyer in winter and its ear tufts grow longer.
